title: Introduce language-affinity lint router and minimal release sentinel
author: Aisha Rahman
description: Motivation: presubmit latency and noisy lint runs were adding churn for polyglot changes and making quiet-window merges brittle. This PR implements a language-affinity lint router that maps changed files to targeted lint profiles (js/ts/python/go/rust) and only runs the minimal plugin set required for the impacted files. It also introduces a minimal release sentinel that aggregates CI health signals (recent flaky-test counts, lint fail rate, quick smoke coverage) and exposes a binary pass/fail to the merge orchestration to avoid noisy merges during unstable windows. Changes: 1) New router: ci/lint/router/* contains the router implementation and a small plugin registry. Router uses file globs and heuristic weightings (diff coverage %, touched lines) to compute a fastpath job set. 2) Profile manifests: ci/lint/profiles/{js,py,go,rs}.yaml declare per-language tooling, cached tool versions, and shard hints. 3) Presubmit orchestration: workflow changes to call router endpoints instead of monolithic lint job; added incremental cache warm step. 4) Release sentinel: ci/release/sentinel service (serverless) that queries recent CI telemetry, cooldown windows, and exposes a /ready endpoint used by the merge bridge action. 5) Small dependency updates: bump eslint-plugin-redwood to 2.4.1, actions/toolcache wrapper to v1.3. CI/noise reductions: default job matrix reduced by ~45% for typical single-language edits (internal sampling on 1k PRs). Backwards compatibility: router falls back to legacy lint profile when it cannot confidently classify file set. Deployment plan: staged rollout — enable router for small teams first via opt-in org label, monitor false-negative rate for 48h, then flip default. A manual rollback is provided (ci/lint/router/rollback.sh) that reverts to previous presubmit workflow. Testing and validation: unit tests for router classification (coverage 92%), integration smoke in staging that runs 120 historical diffs, canary on 5% of new PRs for 24h. Observability: added router classification metric, routed_lint_jobs, drop-in lint_coverage_ratio and sentinel_ready gauge. Checklist: [x] unit tests [x] integration smoke [x] CI matrix sampling and telemetry wiring [x] docs: ci/README.md updated with usage and opt-in flags [x] rollout plan added to Linear ENG-2149. Impact: reduces presubmit cost for mixed repos, improves merge stability during release windows, and creates an extensible hook for future language-specific optimizations. Caveats: some large multi-language monorepos may still trigger full profiles; we keep the legacy fallback for safety.

release_notes: Add language-affinity lint router to reduce unnecessary presubmit lint work and a minimal release sentinel to gate auto-merges during unstable CI windows; opt-in rollout and metrics added.
perf_summary: Sampling on 1k historical PRs indicates median presubmit job count reduced from 7 to 3 for single-language edits (≈45% reduction), CI runtime per PR median reduced by ~38%, infra cost estimate reduction ~22% for presubmit lanes during canary traffic.
rollout_plan: Stage 1: opt-in label for 3 teams (48h), Stage 2: 5% canary of new PRs (24h), Stage 3: default-on for new repos with rollback guard (1w), manual rollback script available if sentinel misclassifies readiness.
notes_for_oncall: If release merges start failing post-rollout, check sentinel telemetry (sentinel_ready gauge) and routed_lint_jobs for unexpected classification spikes; rollback script is ci/scripts/rollback-lint-router.sh.
